column5: scripts/dead-guard-scan.py -- this module's own exercise is through a SUBPROCESS: 8 of its tests drive the shipped CLI with subprocess.run, and sys.settrace is per-interpreter, so tracing under-reports it wholesale. Measured 2026-08-26: of the 29 branches a traced run flagged, only 6 execute when the same functions are driven IN-PROCESS, and spot-reading shows most of the rest ARE reached by the e2e tests. Flags on this file are an artefact of the instrument, not evidence about the code. lib/dead_guard.py stays instrumented -- it IS imported in-process, and it measures clean

scripts/testlib/dead_guard_plugin.py -- the tracer itself. CPython suppresses tracing inside the trace function, so this module is structurally invisible to its own instrument; every branch would read as dead. The one file that cannot measure itself

scripts/claude-hooks/tests/test_bash_guard.py -- NOT a pytest suite by design; its own docstring says so ("hand-rolled asserts, not pytest-collectable -- the guard calls main() at import time, so it is only ever driven via subprocess"). Registering it as instrumentable produced zero traced lines, which the scan reported UNDECIDABLE rather than publishing 400 lines of false flags against the PreToolUse deny-guard

scripts/browser-bridge/tests -- the exemplar guard (_cli_timeout_violations) lives here, but the suite spawns the real browser CLI with a 300s budget per site, so a traced run is far too slow to be re-derivable; measure it on demand with a narrowed selector
scripts/claude-hooks/tests -- the rest of it: ordinary unit suites for the notify/nudge/capture hooks rather than corpus-scanning guards; the two real guards there ARE instrumented above
